exposure: maternal demographics (minoritised ethnicity, age < 20 years, age 40+ years)
obstetric risk factors (primiparity, nonspontaneous vaginal birth modes, urinary retention, postnatal wound breakdown)
outcome: emergency postnatal maternal hospital readmissions related to pregnancy or giving birth within 42 days postpartum
cohort: The study included 6,192,140 women who gave birth in English NHS hospitals from April 2007 to March 2017.
finding: The rate of emergency postnatal maternal readmissions significantly increased from 2.5% in 2008 to 3.4% in 2016, with minoritised ethnicity, age extremes, primiparity, nonspontaneous birth modes, longer postnatal length of stay, urinary retention, and postnatal wound breakdown identified as key risk factors.
mod_finding: Nonspontaneous vaginal birth modes, particularly emergency caesarean sections, were associated with an increased risk of emergency postnatal maternal readmission (aOR 1.86).
